observations:
Torah #129 does not require any new package types that are not already established in the cross-Torah taxonomy. The two packages identified are both well-attested types:

Package 1 (ארץ/אמונה/הצדיק) is a direct instantiation of the 'Faith and Land' package type, which appears across many Torahs (e.g., Torah #9 has ארץ ישראל↔תפלה↔אמונה as a core cluster). The added layer — that the Tzaddik himself is a bechina of ארץ — is a specific expression of a well-known cross-Torah pattern: the Tzaddik is identified with fundamental positive realities (ארץ, אמונה, ראש, שמש, etc.) in many Torahs. The Tzaddik-as-Land identification is specific to this Torah but fits the existing package taxonomy perfectly.

Package 2 (מוח/דעת/תרין רעין) is a variant of the 'Holy Intellect / Mochin' package type that appears in many Torahs. Rebbe Nachman frequently equates מוח, דעת, and various pairs of spiritual companions (תרין רעין דלא מתפרשין is a Zoharic concept appearing in many teachings). No new package taxonomy entry is required.

There is no evil-mirror package in this Torah: the Torah's negative side (the person who lacks will to serve God, who gets 'vomited out' by the Tzaddik/Land) is described behaviorally/functionally rather than through named concept-nodes equated with an evil domain. The vomiting image (כַּאֲשֶׁר קָאָה אֶת הַגּוֹי) is a metaphorical illustration, not a bechina identification of an evil counterpart-cluster. This is consistent with the Torah's short, focused structure — it establishes the positive mechanism (absorption into holiness) and then describes the negative outcome functionally, without naming evil-side bechina nodes.

Conclusion: The teaching's full package structure is captured by two established types — Land/Faith/Tzaddik (good) and Holy Intellect/Mochin (good) — with no new cross-Torah package type emerging.
